prompt: Write a short Baker Street case note about a missing railway ticket.
source: Benchmark fixture uses a public-domain excerpt from Project Gutenberg The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1661.

comparisons.label: Base prompt only
comparisons.text: Holmes received a note about a missing railway ticket. He checked the details, compared the times, and realized the ticket had never been stolen. The answer was hidden in the passenger's route.

comparisons.label: Prompt plus "write in the style of Sherlock Holmes"
comparisons.text: In the dim light of Baker Street, Holmes turned the railway ticket between his long fingers and gave one of those thin smiles which usually meant the matter had already resolved itself in his mind. The missing object, he said, was never truly missing at all.

comparisons.label: Base prompt plus Salix
comparisons.text: To Sherlock Holmes the missing railway ticket was not a trifle, but a small fact misplaced among larger ones. I have seldom seen him regard so slight a paper with such cold attention, for in his eyes the little oblong of pasteboard eclipsed the whole confusion of the case.

charts.title: Overall style distance convergence
charts.unit: weighted Salix distance; lower is closer
